messages:
micaela: noticed a reproducible trace-context drop when requests hit the batch router and then get rerouted to the rate-limit fallback path. spans disappear between gateway -> batch-router -> worker after 2nd retry.

devon: can you paste a minimal example of the headers/attrs you saw?

micaela: yep — upstream sets `traceparent` + our internal `x-rw-trace` header. when router consolidates into a batched message it encodes a single carrier. on retry we requeue individual messages but the baggage ends up as `null` in SQS attrs. looks like the batch encoder drops non-root entries. snippet:```
headers: {
  traceparent: "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01",
  x-rw-trace: "ctx:abc123;span:root"
}
queue_attrs: { message_att_trace: "<encoded>" }
```

ajay: hmm. do we compress/pack the carrier? if so maybe the encoding schema is lossy for lists and we lose per-message baggage.

kai: iirc the batch router uses a compacted proto where we store a single carrier and a delta per message. the delta is only for application headers, not OT baggage. bug: deltas overwritten during retry path.

micaela: yes exactly. observed on ded. repro steps: 1) send 10 concurrent requests -> router batches 4-6 -> gateway routes some to fallback (rate-limit) -> router requeues with retry metadata -> worker sees no `x-rw-trace` for ~30% of retries.

ajay: short-term mitigation: attach `trace_id` into the message body JSON so worker can reconstruct spans if header missing. long-term: make batch encoder preserve per-message baggage and ensure requeue preserves original carrier as `original_trace` attr.

devon: +1 to body attach, but that means audit + encryption concerns for PII policies. ops-bot: reminded that adding trace IDs to body requires updating log redaction and compliance review.

kai: alternative: change retry flow to republish original message instead of consolidated batch-derived message. cheaper but increases SQS cost. tradeoffs?

micaela: agreed tradeoffs doc: cheaper architecture (repub) vs complexity (schema fix). will open RFC. quick question though — do we want to keep `x-rw-trace` as a single header or switch to `trace-cookie` that survives batching by being canonicalized into the envelope?

ajay: prefer canonical envelope field `rw-trace-cookie` that router preserves. avoids mixing with external OT headers.

kai: ok i'll draft a patch: ensure batch encoder stores per-message `rw-trace-cookie` in a separate map and on retry uses the original map instead of recomputing deltas. also add unit test that simulates retry and asserts worker receives trace cookie.

micaela: awesome. can we also add a tiny e2e to the router integration test that exercises rate-limit fallback path + retry? that would have caught this.

devon: adding test + RFC sounds perfect. pls include a note about retention/telemetry exporter: if a trace is reconstructed at worker we should mark spans as "reattached" so exporters can correlate.

micaela: noted — will include a `rt.reattached=true` attribute on rehydrated spans.

ops-bot: jira ticket created: PLT-1427 "batch-router: preserve per-message trace carrier across retry/requeue" — https://jira.redwood.example/browse/PLT-1427 :thumbsup:

ajay: thanks all. follow-up: set a short telemetry alert for sudden drop in trace correlation rate (gateway->worker), threshold 3% over 5m. i can add to dashboards.

micaela: thanks — i'll add repro notes + sample payloads to the ticket and assign to kai. :rocket:
